claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 16 years old and lives with me at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 16 years old, there are specific rules that apply. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit for a child aged 16 or over if they are under 20 and stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, studying A-levels, doing a college course, or in an apprenticeship)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training at the moment. He left school recently, but he has registered with the local careers service to help him figure out what to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. That's actually relevant to your Child Benefit eligibility.

According to the rules, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**When did Alex register with the careers service?** (I need to know if it's been less than or more than 20 weeks since he registered)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been less than 20 weeks - just a couple of months ago actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he claiming any benefits in his own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working 24 hours or more per week, and he's not claiming any benefits in his own right.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, another parent or guardian)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Although Alex is 16 and has left education, he has registered with the local careers service within the last couple of months. Under UK Child Benefit rules, you can continue to claim Child Benefit for **up to 20 weeks** after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training, as long as they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

Since it's been less than 20 weeks since Alex registered, you can continue claiming Child Benefit for him during this period. All other requirements are also met:
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you
- He's not working 24+ hours per week
- He's not claiming benefits in his own right
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**Important note:** The 20-week period is temporary, so if Alex hasn't started approved education, training, or work by the time that period ends, your Child Benefit entitlement for him may stop. If he does start approved education or training before then, you can continue claiming as long as he stays in it (up until he turns 20).
